subject: Targeted regional egress disruption - reroute bridge & validation plan
messages:
From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@nimblepay.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: cloud-support@publiccloud.example
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 22:14:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden 5xx spike from APAC -> US/edge egress failures

Hi Ava,

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and connection timeouts from our APAC traffic to your US/edge endpoints ~21:50 UTC. Latency spikes first, then a surge in token errors. Our engineers see the upstream TCP connections reset and TLS handshakes failing intermittently. Impact is affecting production traffic (payment auth flows) for a subset of users routed through Tokyo and Sydney.

Can Redwood confirm whether there is an egress routing degradation on your side? We need a short-term reroute plan we can apply on our side and any configuration checks to validate. Attaching a minimal log excerpt.

Thanks — Lina
Lina Ortiz
Head of SRE, NimblePay
ops@nimblepay.com

Attachment: nimblepay-logs-1128-snippet.txt (text)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@nimblepay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 22:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike from APAC -> US/edge egress failures

Hi Lina — thanks for the quick report and the log snippet. We're actively investigating.

Immediate notes and actions we will take now:
- Stand up a temporary egress bridge in APAC to route your Tokyo/Sydney traffic to a nearby regional cache (estimated +15-30ms).
- Apply prefix-based routing for NimblePay ingress to steer requests away from the affected peering mesh.
- Provide a validation checklist (attached) you can run client-side to confirm connectivity.

I'll loop in Ben and Olga for the bridge/peering changes and Jordan for validation instructions. We'll confirm times and share the reroute commands.

I'll follow up in ~15 minutes with the plan and a Doc link.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai
Attachment: egress-reroute-checklist.pdf (PDF)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 22:34:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Sudden 5xx spike from APAC -> US/edge egress failures

Team — forwarding NimblePay report. TL;DR: APAC -> US egress seems to be dropping in-flight TLS sessions at our peering layer for a specific subset of prefixes (Tokyo/Sydney). Immediate plan below; callout items in bold.

Planned immediate runbook (execute in this order):
1) Ben: provision temporary APAC egress bridge (gcp-apac-bridge-02) and advertise route for nimblepay prefixes via BGP local-pref to force path through the bridge. Keep community tag: 0xA0. Target up in 10–12 minutes.
2) Olga: confirm firewall/NAT scaling and ensure conntrack entries are not pegged on the bridge instances; increase conntrack_limit on nodes + per-node tcp_keepalive reduction.
3) Jordan + Karthik: prepare validation script (curl/tls handshake with --tlsv1.3 single-sni) and post-deploy smoke checks; coordinate with NimblePay SRE on test window.
4) I will send NimblePay the short client-side reroute they can apply (dns override + prefer local cache endpoints) and the checklist to confirm green.

Please reply in-thread with ETA and add any risk notes. If bridge fails to stabilize in 30 minutes, we will fallback to multi-region rehome and notify NimblePay.

-----Original message attached-----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 22:41:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden 5xx spike from APAC -> US/edge egress failures

Ava — provisioning bridge now. Launching gcp-apac-bridge-02 (n1-standard-4, 2xT4) and pre-warming BGP session.
ETA: BGP up in ~9 minutes; route announcement after validation.
Risk: conntrack pressure possible — will coordinate with Olga on scaling.

I'll post the exact BGP command snippets once the instance has the routable IP.

Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Lina Ortiz <lina.ortiz@nimblepay.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@nimblepay.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx spike from APAC -> US/edge egress failures

Ava / team — confirmed. We applied the DNS override and ran the checklist steps. Traffic now routes through your apac bridge and TLS handshakes remain stable. 5xx rate dropped to baseline within 2 minutes.

Validation artifacts attached (nimblepay-validation-log-1128.csv). We'll keep monitoring but this looks good from our side. Please keep us informed of the root-cause analysis and any long-term mitigation.

Appreciate the rapid response.

— Lina
Lina Ortiz
Head of SRE, NimblePay
Attachment: nimblepay-validation-log-1128.csv (CSV)
